metadata.note: The Utica, Clinton and Binghamton Railroad and its companion the Rome and Clinton, before the New York, Ontario and Western. The UC&B grew out of the Utica City Rail Road, a horse street railway; reorganized Jan 1 1866 as the Utica and Waterville Railroad and renamed the Utica, Clinton and Binghamton Mar 25 1868, it opened piecemeal from the north: a steam-dummy road New Hartford - Clinton by summer 1866 (single source), Deansville Jan 1868, Oriskany Falls 1868, and Randallsville on the Midland main line Sept 26 1870. It never reached Binghamton. Passengers for Utica rode the company's horse cars from New Hartford until a steam line opened Jan 15 1872; no horse-drawn years are drawn (Rule 5). Five operators ran it before the O&W, and each is its own feature (Rule 4): the UC&B itself to July 1871; the New York and Oswego Midland (in receivership from Sept 1873) to Nov 3 1875; the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western 'under agreement' for the Delaware and Hudson Canal Co. to Apr 1 1883; the D&H itself to June 1 1886; then the NYO&W by 35-year sublease, already drawn in nyo_and_w_railway.geojson and not repeated here. The Rome and Clinton (incorporated 1869, opened June 15 1872, leased to the Midland) is drawn only for its one proven passenger year, 1875 [ANCHOR].
sources: https://nashuacitystation.org/history/the-utica-clinton-and-binghamton-railroad-company/ (1929 ICC valuation report on the NYO&W as reproduced section by section: Utica City RR -> Utica & Waterville Jan 1 1866 -> UC&B Mar 25 1868; Randallsville - New Hartford 27 mi opened Sept 26 1870; leased to NY&OM July 1871; New Hartford - Utica 4 mi opened Jan 15 1872; lease to D&H Canal Co. Nov 3 1875 'operated under agreement by the DL&W'; D&H assumes operation Apr 1 1883; sublease to NYO&W June 1 1886)
https://nashuacitystation.org/history/rome-and-clinton-railroad-company/ (Rome & Clinton: incorporated June 3 1869, leased to NY&OM; opened June 15 1872; same later chronology as the UC&B)

Bagg, 1892, p.393-94: horse road to New Hartford 1863, steam dummy New Hartford - Clinton by summer 1866, Deansville Dec 1867, Oriskany Falls 1868, Hamilton and Smith's Valley 1870, steam line into Utica built 1871)
https://www.wgpfoundation.org/historic-markers/deansboro-depot/ (Deansboro depot marker: regular service began Jan 6 1868)

https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/newyorkstaterrs2.pdf (J. Fowler, New York State Railroads (2), SL 202, 10.06.25: sections 83, 90 and 91 mark the Utica Division and Rome Branch stations 'y', 1874 public timetable or 1875 Official Guide)

not_yet_sourced: Passenger service Nov 1875 - June 1886 on Utica - Randallsville (DL&W and D&H eras) is INFERRED from continuity; no timetable, guide or newspaper dated inside those years was found. The NY Railroad Commissioners' annual reports 1880-86 (HathiTrust) give passenger train-miles by company and would settle it.

The DL&W's role 1875-1883 rests on one source (the 1929 ICC valuation via Nashua City Station). If 'operated under agreement' meant D&H-run trains, dlw-utica-randallsville should be recoloured to the D&H and merged with dh-utica-randallsville.

Rome - Clinton is drawn for 1875 only [ANCHOR]. Passenger trains between the June 15 1872 opening and 1874/75, and through the DL&W and D&H years 1875-1886, are not evidenced and are NOT drawn. Fowler's 'y' is either the 1874 public timetable or the 1875 Official Guide; if 1874 is accepted the anchor could be 1874-1875. Local papers (Rome Sentinel, Utica Herald/Observer, Clinton Courier) via nyshistoricnewspapers.org or fultonhistory.com are the place to look.
The 1866 steam-dummy start (New Hartford - Clinton) is single-source (Memorial History of Utica, 1892). If two sources are required, that feature should start in 1868.
Midland lease date: July 1871 (ICC, Pomeroy page) vs about 1872 (Memorial History). 1871 drawn.

Corporate origin conflict: the Memorial History says a Utica, Clinton and Binghamton Company was organized Aug 1862 to build a horse or steam road Clinton - Utica - Whitesboro; the ICC has Utica City RR -> Utica & Waterville (1866) -> UC&B (1868). Affects no drawn year.
Oriskany Falls opening is year-level (1868) only; no month found.
The alignment from New Hartford into Utica, and the Utica terminal, before 1886 are not established; the features draw the later O&W/DL&W-era entry to the O&W Division Street terminal.

EXISTING LAYER, NOT FIXED HERE: nyo_and_w_railway.geojson draws nyow-utica-branch (Randallsville - Utica) and nyow-rome-branch (Clinton - Rome) 1886-1957. The Feb 1952 Official Guide (NYO&W Tables 6 and 8) prints both as 'Freight Service only', so 1951-1957 is overstated on both; on the Utica branch Fowler gives a wartime service into Utica Division Street 'restored 1943>1944' (Division Street the terminus in the 1943 Official Guide), so the passenger end is about 1944, possibly with an undated lapse c.1932-1943. The Rome branch passenger end is unknown, before Sept 1951. The nyow-utica-branch note also calls the 1886 transfer a purchase; per the ICC it was a 35-year sublease.

metadata.horsecar_audit: Excluded under Rule 5: the Utica - New Hartford horse road (fall 1863 to the steam line's opening Jan 15 1872), the horse extension to Whitesboro, and the UC&B's Utica street railway (horse-worked until leased to the Utica Belt Line Street RR Dec 1 1886). The New Hartford - Clinton feature starts with the 1866 steam dummy.

segments.note: The first mechanically worked piece of the line: by the summer of 1866 the company (then the Utica and Waterville Railroad, renamed the Utica, Clinton and Binghamton by special act Mar 25 1868 - a rename, not a change of operator) had a road for steam power from New Hartford to Clinton, 'worked by a dummy' - a steam car built to carry passengers. Passengers for Utica changed at New Hartford to the company's horse cars; that horse section (Utica - New Hartford, from fall 1863 until the steam line opened Jan 15 1872, and on to Whitesboro) is not drawn under Rule 5. THE 1866 START RESTS ON ONE SOURCE (Memorial History of Utica, 1892); no timetable or newspaper confirms it, and the ICC chronology has no event before 1868. The earliest independently attested regular service on the line is Jan 6 1868 at Deansville. Ends July 1871, when the property was leased to the New York and Oswego Midland (an operator change, not an end of service). Headway 480 min (about two trains each way a day) is an estimate; no pre-1886 timetable with times was seen.
sources: Segment-level: start 1866 is single-source - Memorial History of Utica, N.Y. (M.M. Bagg, 1892) p.393-94 (the 'dummy' New Hartford - Clinton by summer 1866), not corroborated; end July 1871 = lease to the NY&OM per the 1929 ICC valuation as reproduced by Nashua City Station. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] The Rome and Clinton Railroad, incorporated June 3 1869 and leased at birth to the Midland, opened to traffic June 15 1872 (ICC; Wikipedia says built 1871 'initially as a coal route'). This is ONE PROVEN YEAR: Fowler's 'New York State Railroads (2)' section 91 marks Kirkland, Clark's Mills, Westmoreland, Bartlett and Rome 'y' - passenger stations in the 1874 Midland public timetable or the 1875 Official Guide (the legends disagree; 1875 is drawn, the research report's drawable span). Passenger trains certainly ran wider both ways, but no other year before 1886 is confirmed: the 1872 opening was to traffic on a line built for coal and is not proof of passengers, and nothing dated was found for the DL&W and D&H years 1875-1886, which are therefore NOT drawn. Do not widen this anchor without dated evidence. The O&W era from 1886 is drawn in nyo_and_w_railway.geojson.
